coldwell.raised.note: Taking the same amount from both sides keeps a balance true. The counterweight answered 4 because 6 take away 2 is 4, and that move works on every balance, not just this one.

countgate.open.note: Undo a story in reverse order. The 3 was added last, so it leaves first: 11 take away 3 is 8. The doubling came first, so it leaves last: half of 8 is 4.

door.open.note: The two numbers the door took multiply to 6 and add to 5. A quadratic that opens this way always hides such a pair; finding it is what factoring means.

draw.bridge.open.note: One pair of numbers had to satisfy two demands at once: the product the balance asked and the sum the gauge asked. Meeting two conditions together is what makes the pair the right one.

launder.done.note: Evaluating a rule is feeding it a number and following the arithmetic. The water agreed with you collar by collar because the rule gives exactly one answer for each x.

lamp.done.note: Multiplication is pouring the same amount again and again. What did not fill a lamp was the remainder, and it stayed visible as darkness.

bellyard.grade.note: A thrown thing rises, slows, turns, and falls along one curve. Reading where the curve crosses a height is the same question as solving for x.

vale.twelve.gate.note: A factorization is a claim about a rectangle: 12 pebbles fill 3 rows of 4 exactly, nothing left over. Any true product of parts rebuilds the whole.

vale.machine.gate.note: Both forms made the same number at every x you fed them. That is what an identity is: two ways of writing one thing, and evaluation can test the claim.

vale.pair.gate.note: The pair multiplies to c and adds to b. Put x = 0 into the factored form and the pair shows itself: (0 + 2)(0 + 3) = 6.

vale.zero.gate.note: Twelve can be made from many pairs, but a product is zero only when a factor is zero. That is the whole reason factoring solves equations.

wood.way.connection.note: The rule you knew was the general rule in disguise. The product target was always a times c; with a = 1 it merely looked like c.

wood.way.merge.note: Taking a number out of a group and taking the shared parcel out of two groups are the same move at two depths. The parcel is a factor the moment you can see it as one thing.

wood.way.pass.note: A fraction root is the mark of a true a-not-1 quadratic. The simpler rule could never have produced this number; that is why the general rule exists.

wood.train.solve.note: The pair 2 and 3: both bars met their marks at once, the product at 6 and the sum at 5.
The pair 3 and 4: of all pairs multiplying to 12, only one also adds to 7. The sum condition is what picks it out.
The pair 3 and 5: checking a pair costs one multiplication and one addition. A wrong pair fails at least one of them, always visibly.
